# git-next Windows metadata cache integration

Source: official crates.io `gix-status` 0.36.0. Archive SHA-256: `42d3174a9f3fb991cf25a7a609ab6c50f19baa7d5f8ce05a48c202f7db4ce3ba`. Cached source was checked byte-for-byte against the verified archive before copying. Upstream MIT and Apache-2.0 licenses remain included.

Share lazy directory listings among the workers of one index/worktree scan. Each worker retains a local lookup map; a shared per-directory initialization cell enumerates that directory once. Enumeration runs outside the directory-map mutex, so unrelated directories can load concurrently. Failed listings or missing names still fall back to live metadata. The existing Windows metadata conversion, reparse/symlink handling, stat/hash validation and `core.fscache` switch are preserved. A fresh scan creates fresh cache state; no process-global cache survives commands or a later checkout clean check.

This only changes in-memory scan resources. Git objects, refs, index format, storage/configuration paths, lock ownership, user settings and credentials are unchanged. There is no data migration or repacking. Rollback is the previous binary. New directory snapshots may represent an earlier instant within a concurrent scan, like other filesystem caches; a command does not provide an atomic filesystem snapshot. A subsequent scan must observe later changes. Conformance, real-edit/EOL visibility, optional locks, read-only index preservation and optimized median/p95 measurements remain required before accepting these bytes.

Published normalized crate metadata omits the upstream path-only test-tools dependency. The standalone cache unit tests use the existing tempfile API through a direct dev dependency; runtime dependencies are unchanged. Tests cover sharing within one scan and fresh metadata in a new scan alongside the original cache/Windows metadata tests.

Use the documented `FileFullDirectoryInfo`/`FILE_FULL_DIR_INFO` query instead of `FileIdBothDirectoryInfo`: status does not consume the latter's file ID or short name. Microsoft's documentation states that the full-directory subset comes from directory entries and avoids the extra MFT information; all required creation/modification times, size, attributes and reparse-tag handling are retained. The 64 KiB aligned buffer and live fallback remain unchanged. An additional unit test compares every cached stat field, type and size with live metadata for ordinary/empty/Unicode files and directories. Existing racy-index content verification stays active. This is an independently implemented Win32 API substitution, with no imported Git implementation. Optimized conformance and paired benchmarks are required before extending the installed checkpoint. See https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winbase/ns-winbase-file_full_dir_info.
